item.title: [DIS] Vellum: Reputation Extension on did:ckb (3 posts)
item.description: Hi @truthixify , I’m thinking of integrating Vellum into Rivet. Developers could link their did:ckb and display their verified claims alongside their Rivet passport. Does your current SDK/API support this, and would you be open to a small Testnet integration? Yes! Let’s do this. Send me a DM on telegram so we can discuss the details. Makes sense, thanks. Since v1 only says the campaign hit its goal and finalized, with the total, I’m fine turning it on as is and leaving the judgement to whoever reads the claim. item.title: [DIS] RIVET: Decentralized GitHub Backup, Timestamping and Restore on CKB (1 posts)
item.description: Rivet Milestone 2: CLI Restore Tooling and Hardening Delivery update · November 21, 2026 · CKB Testnet Implementation and project acceptance testing for Rivet’s second grant milestone are complete. Milestone 2 delivers a published cross-platform CLI, independent Exact Restore, Attribution Restore with signed commit mappings, separate mapping commitments on CKB Testnet, stronger backup commitments, and improvements to transaction recovery, backup-job coordination, and Auto Sync reliability. The current published preview is cli-v0.1.0-rc.4. It includes the unchanged-backup waiting fix and works with the deployed server’s duplicate-snapshot protection. item.title: [DIS] KeyMe — CKB's PSBT: Open Air-Gapped Signing and the First DIY Hardware (1 posts)
item.description: Very promising initiative, just two questions with PSCT v0, one, combine() only merges signatures for an identical transaction. item.title: RFC draft: Lock Proof, proving control of a CKB lock (3 posts)
item.description: LusoCryptoLabs: Which locks does your backend need to accept? of course this is wallet binding we’re talking about so ideally all locks getting supported is very beneficial and that’s why I asked. Unless it can be used for something else i’m not aware yet? All locks is what it is built for. The verifier runs the lock itself in CKB-VM, so one code path covers every lock that signs the transaction hash; the only lock-specific check refuses Omnilock in administrator mode. A port has no lock to start from, and it would be checked against the 17 signed proofs in tests/vectors (section 13 of the spec says how each was signed). Not covered: relative or not-yet-matured time conditions, locks...

item.title: DAO提案公平性疑问？ (11 posts)
item.description: Fai: And the result? Some people left in disappointment, the project ultimately fell apart, and the DAO wasted precious treasury funds — a lesson that left everyone worse off. Hey @Fai, the integration is on hold, not abandoned: I covered the details in the Rosen thread. The DAO paid only the first milestone: $15k for the technical assessment and development plan, public in the tracker. The other $50k comes only with the testbed and mainnet releases: no release, no payment. The work since then caught a bridge risk before any CKB user funds were exposed. About that risk: each Guard (the operators who jointly sign bridge payouts) trusts one data source for deposits, by default a public RPC....
